merger_description:
Ctrl Bidco Pty Ltd (**ctrl:cyber**) proposes to acquire 100% of the issued shares in Razilio Pty Ltd, trading as Razilio (**Razilio**), from Horatio Investments Pty Ltd as trustee for Horatio Investment Holdings (the **Acquisition**).

ctrl:cyber is an Australian-based provider of end-to-end cybersecurity, privacy and AI-governance services, servicing clients across Australia. Its brands include ‘ctrl:cyber’ (its core brand) and ‘elevenM’ (a business that provides privacy, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence and data governance solutions).

Razilio is an Australian-based boutique cybersecurity and cyber resilience consulting business, servicing clients predominantly in New South Wales, Victoria and Queensland. Its brands include ‘Razilio’ (its core brand) and ‘Meerkat’ (a continuous exposure/attack-surface monitoring product).

Both ctrl:cyber and Razilio provide cybersecurity governance, risk and compliance advisory, cyber incident response planning and support, cyber threat detection and defence posture monitoring, and cyber awareness and training.

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. the parties’ combined share in the supply of cybersecurity
services to customers in Australia is low and the increase in
share of supply arising from the Acquisition would be small
b. there are several alternative suppliers of cybersecurity
services to customers in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
